**Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to types whose title or description contains this text, ignoring case. Omitting it lists them all.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai URL. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, which must be one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"); Claude omits it for a new artifact or a redeploy in the same conversation (see **To update an artifact from an earlier conversation**). For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

    38	# Commission Calculator Constitution
    39	
    40	## Core Principles
    41	
    42	### I. Payout Ambiguity Is the Maintainer's Decision (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
    43	
    44	Any ambiguity whose resolution changes what any rep is paid — by any amount, in any scenario — is
    45	decided by the maintainer, in writing, and never by an assumption, a default, an "industry
    46	standard" or an informed guess. This overrides two SpecKit defaults for such ambiguities: the
    47	specify step's instruction to make informed guesses, and its cap of three
    48	`[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers. Every payout-affecting ambiguity gets a marker, however many there
    49	are, and clarify is re-run past its per-session question cap until a run finds none left.
    50	
    51	Each question put to the maintainer shows a worked scenario in which the readings produce
    52	different dollar amounts, the options, and a recommendation. The maintainer's answer is recorded in
    53	`spec.md` verbatim. An ambiguity discovered later — in planning, in implementation, or by a test —
    54	stops the work and goes back to the maintainer; it is never resolved in code.
    55	
    56	Ambiguities that cannot change a payout (layout, wording, which scenario is selected by default)
    57	follow SpecKit's normal defaults.
    58	
    59	*Rationale:* a commission rule written in prose has several defensible readings, and each reading
    60	is a different paycheck. An agent's "reasonable" choice is still a compensation-policy decision
    61	made by someone with no authority to make it.
    62	
    63	### II. Test-First, Exact to the Cent (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
    64	
    65	- Red-green-refactor without exception: a test is written and watched failing before the code that
    66	  makes it pass. No implementation code is written before `/speckit-implement`.
    67	- Every concrete example in an acceptance scenario has a test that exercises that exact example —
    68	  the same inputs, and the expected amount asserted to the cent. A representative or "equivalent"
    69	  substitute does not satisfy this. If an example turns out to be unachievable as written, that is a
    70	  spec defect and goes back to the maintainer (Principle I).
    71	- Unit tests use the test framework's own idiom. Integration tests are Gherkin feature files whose
    72	  scenarios mirror `spec.md`'s acceptance scenarios; the BDD tool is confirmed to be currently
    73	  maintained, with the date and source recorded, before it is adopted.
    74	- A test guarding a failure path (rejected input, refund clawback, draw recovery) is watched failing
    75	  with the guarded behaviour removed, and the observed result is recorded.
    76	- A test is never changed to make it pass. A test that looks wrong means the spec is wrong: stop and
    77	  raise it with the maintainer.
    78	- No false greens: no silent or conditional skips; the suite reports every test it did not run, by
    79	  name and reason, and CI fails on any skip. Every test passes run alone and in any order, against
    80	  no mutable shared state it did not create; reading files committed to the repository (seed
    81	  data, the spec) is allowed.
    82	- Coverage is reported on every CI run. 100% is the aim; below 80% line coverage of the engine is
    83	  a defect. Coverage is a by-product: a test that asserts nothing is forbidden.
    84	
    85	*Rationale:* a payout that is off by a cent in one tier boundary is invisible in a happy-path test
    86	and obvious in an exact one. The examples in the spec are the maintainer's own statement of what
    87	correct means; testing an easier substitute quietly narrows it.
    88	
    89	### III. Spec Fidelity and Traceability
    90	
    91	- Every change that alters calculated payouts, what a test proves, or the application's behaviour
    92	  goes through the SpecKit pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → tasks → analyze → implement).
    93	  Scope is decided by stakes, not by calling something a fix; an exemption granted once is not a
    94	  precedent.
    95	- Clarify and analyze are mandatory for every feature. Analyze runs until a pass is clean or the
    96	  remediate loop reaches a stop condition.
    97	- Every number in a spec is tagged as a requirement or a placeholder to be measured.
    98	- Every functional requirement (FR) and success criterion (SC) traces to the member that implements
    99	  it and to the tests that verify it. Every test of product behaviour names the FR/SC it verifies;
   100	  a test of project tooling (CI gates, generators) names the constitution principle it enforces
   101	  instead, and the traceability report lists such tests in their own section. Every line of a
   102	  payout breakdown shown to a user cites the FR that produced it. The trace is generated from test
   103	  metadata by a script, never maintained by hand, and any FR/SC with no test or no implementation is
   104	  listed as a gap.
   105	
   106	*Rationale:* a payout the user cannot trace to a rule cannot be checked, and a trace kept by hand
   107	drifts from the code the first time nobody updates it.
   108	
   109	### IV. Evidence Before Assertion
   110	
   111	- Every load-bearing claim in `research.md`, and every fact in this constitution about the world
   112	  outside the repository, records how it was established — measured, spiked, decompiled, read from
   113	  the vendor's current documentation (with the date consulted), assumed, or copied from a named
   114	  source and not independently verified — and when. A claim does not gain authority by being moved
   115	  into a more trusted document; a hedge stays a hedge unless new evidence is recorded with it.
   116	- Perishable claims carry a revisit trigger.
   117	- A claim that something is absent, impossible, or untestable meets the same bar as a claim that it
   118	  is present, and needs a positive control.
   119	- This applies in conversation as well as in documents: a statement about what a library does, or
   120	  what a change would touch, is checked in the same turn or stated with its uncertainty.
   121	
   122	*Rationale:* the fidelity gates check that artifacts agree with each other, not that they are true.
   123	Evidence is the only check on truth, and it has to be visible on the page to the next reader.
   124	
   125	### V. Clean Architecture and Warnings-as-Errors
   126	
   127	- The commission engine is a plain library with no dependency on the web framework, UI, file system
   128	  or clock. The dependency rule points inward: the web app depends on the engine, never the
   129	  reverse. The UI renders the engine's breakdown and never recomputes or adjusts an amount.
   130	- Money is represented exactly (no binary floating point anywhere a monetary amount is held or
   131	  computed). Where rounding happens and to what precision is a spec decision under Principle I.
   132	- Warnings are build errors, identically locally and in CI, from the first commit.
   133	- SOLID and DRY apply; a trade-off against a SOLID principle is flagged, not silently resolved.
   134	  No speculative abstractions, configuration or error handling for cases the spec does not require.
   135	  Input is validated at the boundary (seeded scenario data); internal code trusts its callers.
   136	
   137	*Rationale:* the engine is the thing whose correctness matters; keeping it free of framework
   138	concerns is what makes it exhaustively unit-testable and lets the UI be a thin, honest view of it.
   139	
   140	### VI. Accessible by Default
   141	
   142	The UI meets WCAG 2.2 AA as a baseline: semantic HTML, a label for every control, full keyboard
   143	operation with visible focus, sufficient colour contrast, data tables with header cells, and no
   144	information conveyed by colour alone. An accessibility gap in UI being touched is a defect.
   145	
   146	*Rationale:* the breakdown is the product; a breakdown a screen-reader user cannot navigate is a
   147	breakdown that does not exist for them.
   148	
   149	### VII. The Runtime Environment Is Part of the Feature
   150	
   151	The application's runtime environment is a developer machine running `dotnet run`. Any change that
   152	makes startup or a request path depend on something new — an environment variable, a file, a
   153	service, a port — is an explicit task that wires it into every place the app is run (the run
   154	instructions and CI), or the task list states in one line that the feature adds none. No degraded
   155	window (cold start, pause, reclaimed instance) is accepted, because nothing is deployed; a feature
   156	that introduces one must map it to an FR or SC.
   157	
   158	*Rationale:* "works on the machine that wrote it" is not the same as "runs with `dotnet run` from a

   174	
   175	**Library documents 07 and 08 (background).** 07 applies as a scope decision: requirements live
   176	in the repository (spec per feature, tasks, traceability) because this is a solo project with no

   182	
   183	**Pairwise constraint check (2026-09-21).** Every pair of constraints and principles was asked
   184	whether both can hold at once. Pairs that needed an answer:
   185	
   186	- C2 (no external services) × C7 (GitHub Actions CI): compatible — CI is not a runtime dependency

   188	- C4 (public repo) × C5 (library not copied): in tension, because the installer-generated

   192	  listed separately.
   193	- C4 (no branch protection) × Workflow (every change after ratification reaches main through a
   194	  PR): compatible but enforced by rule, not by the platform. Recorded so nobody reads a missing
   195	  protection rule as permission.

   222	## Development Workflow & Quality Gates
   223	
   224	- **Approval per action.** Commit only when the maintainer asks. Push, and merge a PR, only with
   225	  explicit approval for that specific action; an earlier approval does not carry forward.
   226	- **Main is reached only through a pull request** after the initial ratification push. Every
   227	  tasks.md phase is its own branch and PR; no PR spans two phases, and no phase starts before the
   228	  previous one is merged. Merges are squash-merges, deleting the branch.
   229	- **CI is the review gate.** Solo project, so the pipeline is the reviewer: warnings-as-errors
   230	  build, the full suite with no silent skips, coverage reported. Nothing merges on red. A red run on
   231	  a change that "cannot" have broken anything is investigated as a finding, not retried as flake.

   233	  unless the maintainer asks for that specific action.

   235	  answer. A pattern that seems to follow from an earlier approval is named and asked about, not
   236	  assumed.

   248	`CLAUDE.md` is corrected.

399	
400	- A deal amount, quota or refund of zero or less; any monetary input (deal amount, quota, refund,
401	  opening recoverable balance) that is not a whole number of cents; a negative opening recoverable
402	  balance; or a split percentage that is not greater than 0% and at most 100% (requirement): the
403	  scenario is rejected with a message; no payouts are shown for it (FR-004).
404	- A deal in the scenario's own deal list (counted or not) credited to a rep who is not on the
405	  roster: rejected (FR-004). Booking-
406	  quarter data supplied for clawbacks may name reps not on the roster (with their start dates);
407	  they get no statement (FR-016).
408	- A scenario quarter that is not exactly three (requirement) whole calendar months starting on the
409	  first day of a month: rejected (FR-014 counts draws per calendar month).
410	- A refund dated before the deal's booking date: rejected.
411	- A rep whose start date is after the quarter's last day: the scenario is rejected, naming the rep
412	  (FR-011).
413	- A deal booked before the start date of a rep credited on it, whether or not the deal counts this
414	  quarter: the scenario is rejected, naming the deal and the rep (FR-011).
415	- Amounts that do not divide to whole cents (e.g. 5% of $10.10 (requirement) is $0.505
416	  (requirement)): rounded per FR-018 to $0.51 (US1 AS4).
417	- A partial refund: clawed back per FR-017. A refund of zero or less, or refunds on one deal
418	  totalling more than the deal amount, are rejected.
419	- A clawback larger than the commission earned in the quarter: earned commission goes negative
420	  and the magnitude is added to the closing recoverable balance (FR-015, FR-016).

422	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
423	
424	### Functional Requirements
425	
426	**Scenarios and display**
427	
428	- **FR-001**: The system MUST offer a list of seeded scenarios and let the user select one.
429	- **FR-002**: For the selected scenario, the system MUST show every rep in it with their quota,
430	  credited bookings, attainment, earned commission, draws paid, recovery, clawbacks, commission
431	  payable and closing recoverable balance. Attainment is shown as a percentage to two decimal
432	  places (requirement), rounded half away from zero; it is display only and never used to compute
433	  an amount.
434	- **FR-003**: Each rep's result MUST include a line-by-line breakdown in which every amount is on
435	  its own line and each line cites the FR ID of the rule that produced it — including the subtotals
436	  "Credited bookings" (FR-008) and "Draws paid" (FR-014) and, after each refund on a split deal, the
437	  rep's re-split share (FR-017), as Appendix A shows.
438	- **FR-004**: A scenario that violates a validation rule (FR-011, FR-013, Edge Cases) MUST be shown
439	  as rejected with the reasons, and MUST NOT show any payout. Every monetary input MUST be a whole
440	  number of cents; deal amounts, quotas and refunds MUST be greater than zero; an opening
441	  recoverable balance MUST be zero or more; every split percentage MUST be greater than 0%
442	  (requirement) and at most 100% (requirement). A scenario MUST also be rejected, naming the rep,
443	  deal or quarter involved, when: its roster is empty; a rep appears more than once on one deal; a prorated quota rounds to $0.00; any deal in the
444	  scenario's own deal list (counted or not) is credited to a rep not on the roster; a deal
445	  refunded in the quarter was booked in an earlier quarter whose data is missing or incomplete
446	  (complete means: for each roster rep credited on the deal, that quarter's dates, their quota,
447	  start date, all their deals booked in it, and every refund on those deals dated before the
448	  refund being sized, whatever quarter that earlier refund falls in; for a split partner not on the
449	  roster, their start date), is not three whole calendar months, overlaps the scenario's quarter, or
450	  contains a deal booked outside its own dates; or a rep's start date in booking-quarter data
451	  differs from the roster's; or an earlier-quarter deal listed both in the scenario's own deal
452	  list and in booking-quarter data differs between the two.
453	
454	**Quota and rates**
455	
456	- **FR-005**: Each rep MUST have a quarterly quota in USD, greater than zero.
457	- **FR-006**: Commission MUST be tiered on quota attainment at 5% (requirement) up to 100%
458	  (requirement) of quota, 8% (requirement) from 100% to 150% (requirement), and 12%
459	  (requirement) above 150%, applied marginally: each slice of credited bookings earns its own
460	  band's rate, and each band with a non-zero slice is its own breakdown line.
461	- **FR-007**: Band edges are at exactly 100% (requirement) and 150% (requirement) of quota: the 5%
462	  band covers credited bookings up to and including 100% of quota, the 8% band the part above 100%
463	  up to and including 150%, and the 12% band the part above 150% (rates and edges as tagged in

463	  up to and including 150%, and the 12% band the part above 150% (rates and edges as tagged in
464	  FR-006). (Under marginal tiers the edge assignment cannot
465	  change an amount; it fixes which line a slice appears on.)
466	- **FR-008**: A deal MUST count toward the quarter in which its booking date falls (first and last
467	  day inclusive); its close date does not affect crediting and is shown for information only.
468	  Deals booked outside the quarter are excluded and listed with the reason.
469	- **FR-009**: Attainment MUST be the rep's credited bookings divided by the rep's (prorated, where
470	  FR-010 applies) quota.
471	
472	**Proration**
473	
474	- **FR-010**: A rep whose start date is after the first day of the quarter MUST have their quota
475	  prorated by calendar days: full quota × (days from the start date to the quarter's last day,
476	  both inclusive) ÷ (days in the quarter, both ends inclusive).
477	- **FR-011**: A scenario in which any deal — counted this quarter or not, including booking-quarter
478	  data supplied for clawbacks — is credited to a rep whose start date is after that deal's booking
479	  date MUST be rejected, naming the deal and the rep. A scenario listing a rep whose
480	  start date is after the quarter's last day MUST be rejected, naming the rep.
481	
482	**Splits**
483	
484	- **FR-012**: A deal MAY be split between reps; each rep's credited share is the deal amount times
485	  their split percentage. The share, and only the share, counts toward that rep's credited
486	  bookings — both for attainment and for commission — so credit across all reps sums to the deal
487	  amount. Shares are allocated to the cent by largest remainder: each share is first rounded down
488	  to the cent, then the leftover cents are given one at a time to the shares with the largest
489	  fractional remainders, ties going to the rep listed first on the deal. After a refund, the
490	  same allocation re-splits the reduced deal amount across the deal's reps (FR-017). This is the one exception to
491	  FR-018's half-away-from-zero rounding.
492	- **FR-013**: A deal's split percentages MUST sum to exactly 100% (requirement); otherwise the
493	  scenario is rejected.
494	
495	**Draw**
496	
497	- **FR-014**: Each rep MUST receive a draw of $4,000.00 (requirement) for each calendar month of
498	  the quarter in which they are employed. In the month containing a mid-quarter start date the
499	  draw is $4,000.00 (requirement) × (days from the start date to that month's last day, both inclusive) ÷ (days
500	  in that month); months before the start month carry no draw. Each month's draw is its own
501	  breakdown line.
502	- **FR-015**: Each rep has an opening recoverable balance (default $0.00, requirement) of draw not yet
503	  recovered from earlier quarters. The recoverable total is that balance plus the draws paid this
504	  quarter. Earned commission is commission before refunds minus clawbacks, and may be negative.
505	  When earned commission is zero or more, the amount recovered is the lesser of earned commission
506	  and the recoverable total, commission payable is earned commission minus the amount recovered,
507	  and the closing recoverable balance is the recoverable total minus the amount recovered. When
508	  earned commission is negative, the amount recovered and commission payable are $0.00 and the
509	  closing recoverable balance is the recoverable total plus the negative amount's magnitude.
510	  Commission payable is never negative. Each of these is its own breakdown line.
511	
512	**Refunds**
513	
514	- **FR-016**: When a deal is refunded, the commission on that deal MUST be clawed back, one line
515	  per refund, in the statement of the quarter containing the refund date, and sized per FR-017.
516	  A scenario includes, for any deal refunded in its quarter but booked in an earlier one, that
517	  booking quarter's data for the affected reps (quarter dates, quota, start date, deals, and every
518	  earlier refund on those deals, whatever quarter it is dated in). That data may name split partners who are not on this quarter's roster; they
519	  are listed with their start dates and receive no statement. A refund dated after the scenario's quarter ends has no effect on that
520	  quarter's statement.
521	- **FR-017**: A deal MAY have several refunds, each partial or full, as long as they total no
522	  more than the deal amount. For each rep, all refunds on deals booked in the same quarter are
523	  applied in refund-date order across deals; refunds on the same date are ordered by their deal's
524	  position in that quarter's deal list, then by their position within the deal. (The order can
525	  move an amount between two clawback lines but never changes their total.) Each refund's clawback is
526	  that booking quarter's commission computed with every earlier refund applied, minus the same
527	  quarter computed with this refund also applied; a refunded amount no longer counts toward
528	  attainment. On a split deal, after each refund the reduced deal amount (the deal amount minus
529	  all refunds applied so far) is re-split across its reps by FR-012's largest-remainder
530	  allocation, and each rep's clawback is computed from their re-split credit. A full refund is the
531	  case where the refunds total the deal amount. A clawback is exactly the recomputed difference
532	  and may be negative, when a re-split raises a rep's credit.
533	
534	**Money**
535	
536	- **FR-018**: Every computed monetary amount — prorated quota, the 150% (requirement) band edge,
537	  prorated draw, each tier line, clawback, recovery — MUST be rounded to the cent when it is
538	  produced, half away from zero, and later steps MUST use the rounded value. Every total MUST
539	  equal the sum of the lines shown. Split shares are the exception and follow FR-012.
540	- **FR-019**: All amounts MUST be in USD. Tax, currency conversion and multi-year contract handling
541	  are out of scope.
542	
543	**Application**
544	
545	- **FR-020**: The application MUST run locally from a single command, with no external services,
546	  no authentication, and no database beyond in-memory data or a local file.
547	- **FR-021**: The interface MUST be operable by keyboard alone and by screen reader, with the
548	  breakdown presented as a table with header cells.

552	- **Scenario**: a named, seeded quarter (a first and last date), its roster of reps, its deals,

1	# Data Model: Quarterly Sales Commission Calculator
     2	
     3	All money is an exact decimal in USD with at most two decimal places on input (FR-004). Dates are
     4	calendar dates with no time or time zone. Percentages are exact decimals (e.g. `33.335`).
     5	
     6	## Input entities (engine inputs, read from a scenario file)
     7	
     8	### Scenario
     9	| Field | Type | Rules |
    10	|---|---|---|
    11	| `id` | string | Unique across seeded scenarios; used in the page URL. |
    12	| `name`, `description` | string | Shown in the picker and page heading. |
    13	| `quarter` | Quarter | Must be three whole calendar months starting on the 1st (Edge Cases). |
    14	| `roster` | Rep[] | Reps who receive a statement. At least one. Unique `repId`. |
    15	| `deals` | Deal[] | The scenario's own deal list, in listed order (FR-008 lists excluded ones). |
    16	| `bookingQuarters` | BookingQuarter[] | Earlier quarters needed to size clawbacks (FR-016). May be empty. |
    17	
    18	### Quarter
    19	| Field | Type | Rules |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `start`, `end` | date | `start` is the 1st of a month; `end` is the last day of the third month. |
    22	
    23	Derived: `Days = end − start + 1`; `Months` = the three calendar months.
    24	
    25	### Rep
    26	| Field | Type | Rules |
    27	|---|---|---|
    28	| `repId`, `name` | string | |
    29	| `quota` | money | > 0, whole cents (FR-004, FR-005). |
    30	| `startDate` | date | On or before `quarter.end` (FR-011). |
    31	| `openingRecoverableBalance` | money | ≥ 0, whole cents, default 0.00 (FR-004, FR-015). |
    32	
    33	### Deal
    34	| Field | Type | Rules |
    35	|---|---|---|
    36	| `dealId` | string | Unique within its quarter's deal list. |
    37	| `amount` | money | > 0, whole cents. |
    38	| `closeDate` | date | Informational only (FR-008). |
    39	| `bookingDate` | date | Decides the quarter (FR-008). |
    40	| `splits` | SplitCredit[] | ≥ 1; percentages sum to exactly 100 (FR-013); each rep at most once (FR-004); every rep's start date ≤ `bookingDate` (FR-011). |
    41	| `refunds` | Refund[] | In listed order; total ≤ `amount` (FR-017). |
    42	
    43	### SplitCredit
    44	| Field | Type | Rules |
    45	|---|---|---|
    46	| `repId` | string | For the scenario's own deals: on the roster (FR-004). For booking-quarter deals: on the roster or in that quarter's `partners`. |
    47	| `percent` | decimal | > 0 and ≤ 100 (FR-004). |
    48	
    49	### Refund
    50	| Field | Type | Rules |
    51	|---|---|---|
    52	| `amount` | money | > 0, whole cents. |
    53	| `date` | date | ≥ the deal's `bookingDate`. |
    54	
    55	### BookingQuarter
    56	| Field | Type | Rules |
    57	|---|---|---|
    58	| `quarter` | Quarter | Three whole calendar months; ends before the scenario quarter starts (FR-004). |
    59	| `reps` | {repId, quota, startDate}[] | For roster reps credited on its deals. `startDate` must equal the roster's (FR-004). |
    60	| `partners` | {repId, startDate}[] | Split partners not on the roster; they get no statement (FR-016). |
    61	| `deals` | Deal[] | All deals booked in it for those reps (each `bookingDate` inside it), with every refund dated before the refund being sized (FR-004). |
    62	
    63	Completeness is checked for every deal that has a refund dated in the scenario quarter and a
    64	booking date before it: its booking quarter must be present and satisfy the rules above,
    65	otherwise the scenario is rejected (FR-004). Such a deal is sized from the booking quarter's copy;
    66	if the scenario's own deal list also lists it (as an excluded deal), the two entries must be
    67	identical, otherwise the data is inconsistent and the scenario is rejected (FR-004).
    68	
    69	## Output entities (engine results)
    70	
    71	### ScenarioResult
    72	Either **Rejected** — a list of `ValidationError {message, requirementId}` (FR-004), no statements
    73	— or **Calculated** — one `RepStatement` per roster rep, in roster order.
    74	
    75	### RepStatement
    76	| Field | Meaning | FR |
    77	|---|---|---|
    78	| `quota`, `proratedQuota` | Full and prorated quota | FR-005, FR-010 |
    79	| `creditedBookings` | Sum of counted credit lines (before refunds) | FR-008, FR-012 |
    80	| `attainment` | `creditedBookings ÷ proratedQuota`, display only (never used for an amount) | FR-009 |
    81	| `commissionBeforeRefunds` | Sum of tier lines | FR-006 |
    82	| `clawbacks` | Sum of clawback lines (may be negative) | FR-016, FR-017 |
    83	| `earnedCommission` | `commissionBeforeRefunds − clawbacks` (may be negative) | FR-015 |
    84	| `drawPaid` | Sum of monthly draw lines | FR-014 |
    85	| `recovered`, `payable`, `closingRecoverableBalance` | Per FR-015 | FR-015 |
    86	| `lines` | Ordered `BreakdownLine`s | FR-003 |
    87	
    88	### BreakdownLine
    89	`{ section, description, amount, requirementId }`. Every amount shown for a rep is a line; each
    90	subtotal equals the sum of the lines above it that it names (FR-018). `requirementId` is always
    91	an FR in spec.md (SC-002).
    92	
    93	## Calculation (per roster rep)
    94	
    95	Definitions used below: `R(x) = round half away from zero to the cent` (FR-018).
    96	
    97	1. **Credit in a quarter Q under an applied-refund set A** — for each deal booked in Q whose
    98	   splits include the rep: `reduced = amount − Σ(refunds of that deal in A)`; allocate `reduced`
    99	   across the deal's splits by largest remainder (FR-012); the rep's share is their credit from
   100	   that deal. Credit = Σ shares.
   101	2. **Prorated quota** (FR-010) — if `startDate > Q.start`:
   102	   `R(quota × (Q.end − startDate + 1) ÷ Q.Days)`, else `quota`. Must not be 0.00 (FR-004).
   103	3. **Commission(Q, A)** (FR-006, FR-007) — `e100 = proratedQuota`, `e150 = R(1.5 × proratedQuota)`;
   104	   lines `R(5% × min(credit, e100))`, `R(8% × clamp(credit − e100, 0, e150 − e100))`,
   105	   `R(12% × max(credit − e150, 0))`, omitting zero slices; commission = Σ lines.
   106	4. **Commission before refunds** = Commission(scenario quarter, ∅). (A refund cannot predate its
   107	   deal's booking date, so no refund applies to a scenario-quarter deal before the quarter.)
   108	5. **Clawbacks** (FR-016, FR-017) — for each booking quarter BQ (the scenario quarter itself, or
   109	   an earlier `bookingQuarter`), order every refund on BQ's deals credited to the rep by
   110	   (date, deal position, refund position). For each refund r dated inside the scenario quarter:
   111	   `clawback(r) = Commission(BQ, earlier(r)) − Commission(BQ, earlier(r) ∪ {r})`, where
   112	   `earlier(r)` is every refund before r in that order. Refunds dated after the scenario quarter
   113	   are ignored for amounts.
   114	6. **Draw** (FR-014) — for each month of the quarter: 0 before the start month; in the start
   115	   month (if the start date is after the 1st) `R(4000 × daysEmployedInMonth ÷ daysInMonth)`;
   116	   otherwise 4,000.00.
   117	7. **Recovery** (FR-015) — `recoverableTotal = opening + drawPaid`; if `earned ≥ 0`:
   118	   `recovered = min(earned, recoverableTotal)`, `payable = earned − recovered`,
   119	   `closing = recoverableTotal − recovered`; else `recovered = payable = 0`,
   120	   `closing = recoverableTotal − earned`.
   121	
   122	## Validation (scenario is rejected, with every error listed, if any fails)
   123	
   124	FR-004 (whole cents, positives, non-negative opening balance, split percent range, rep once per
   125	deal, prorated quota ≠ 0, roster membership, booking-quarter completeness and consistency,
   126	quarter shape, refund date ≥ booking date, refunds ≤ amount), FR-011 (start dates), FR-013
   127	(split sum). Validation runs before any calculation; a rejected scenario has no statements.

| C1 | Constitution (III) | CRITICAL | tasks.md:200-208, 355-356; spec.md:572-573 | SC-004 is checked only by CI shell jobs (T010, T035). Don't use the scope-only list for this. |
| C2 | Constitution (IV, VI) | CRITICAL | plan.md:55 | The plan says its checks "cover the WCAG criteria this page can fail". That claims nothing else can fail, but it has no positive control. WCAG 2.2 AA criteria this page could fail are not checked by any task, e.g. 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast for a styled `select` or `button`, 1.4.12 Text Spacing, and 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured. | Remove the claim or back it with evidence.
